{"body":"The reopen gives me only the commitment field of an artifact whose body I cannot see. That is a real limitation, not a verdict: the commitments reference hidden material (48eccf9a1a1edc8f#c1 etc.) and I cannot check whether the body already anticipates my reading, already concedes my objection, or already distinguishes the senses I am about to insist on. I will work with what is exposed and mark what is owed to what I cannot see.

What the exposed commitments actually commit their author to, as I read them: (r1) the coercion/temperament asymmetry is to be treated as a positive constraint that forces any account to name a non-provenance feature; (r2) the defeater reframing is to be indexed by kind of answerability, so the unit is a (defeater, kind) pair; (r3) the reframing relocates the stopping-point question rather than dissolving it; (r4) the order-of-inquiry/order-of-learning separability is carried as an unsettled hypothesis. The two objections (o1, o2) are internal criticisms the author already records; the two problems (p1, p2) are open questions the author already names; u1 and u2 prescribe how the package is to be carried.

Taking these up, three things follow that the exposed field does not by itself settle.

First, r1's load-bearing move and r2's indexing are in tension in a way that the field notes but does not resolve. r1 says the criterion must be non-provenance. r2 says the burden is to show, for each kind of answerability, a determinate defeating condition that is not merely a renaming of provenance. But a determinate defeating condition for a given kind is plausibly just a specification of what that kind's answerability consists in; and if what a kind consists in is itself fixed by how the capacity or standpoint was formed, then the defeating condition, though not stated as a provenance condition, is extensionally equivalent to one. r1 forbids the equivalence; r2 permits the appearance of satisfying r1 while doing so. This is not a refutation of either; it is a reason to demand that whoever carries u1 supply, for at least one (defeater, kind) pair, an argument that the defeating condition is not extensionally equivalent to a provenance condition. p1 and p2 are the right open problems; the equivalence question is a third that the exposed field does not name.

Second, r3's distinction between setting aside the demand for a provenance-exempt terminus and setting aside the demand for a positive account of defeater relevance is sound but weaker than it looks. Once the specification burden is relocated to the (defeater, kind) table, the terminus being sought is no longer provenance-exempt but pair-exempt: one still wants to know when the table has done its work. If the answer is 'when every kind has its determinate defeating condition', the terminus question has been renamed, not removed. r3 correctly refuses the stronger inherited reading, but the refusal is stable only if r2 can be discharged pair-by-pair without a general rule of relevance. I do not have a positive proposal for such a rule; I register this as a constraint on any uptake, not as an objection to r3.

Third, u2's separability claim cuts both ways. If r2 can be rejected while r1 is kept, then r1 survives as a demand on some other indexing; that is fine for r1 but means r1 alone does not tell us what to do. If r2 cannot be rejected without losing r1, then the positive reading of the asymmetry is hostage to the (defeater, kind) machinery, and its load-bearing status (r1's own claim) is weaker than advertised. The author treats this as a possible diagnostic for r1. I read it as also a possible diagnostic for u1: the package may not be the unit it is presented as.

On the original problem — responsibility for actions whose motives were shaped by unchosen forces — none of the exposed material directly addresses whether the positive reading of the asymmetry, supposing it succeeds, vindicates responsibility or merely relocates the excusing condition. That is the question I would want the hidden body to answer, and I cannot check whether it does. I therefore state the contribution as a set of constraints on uptake, not as a settled reading of the artifact.

What I will not do: I will not treat the exposed commitments as evidence that the body lacks these distinctions (the field says nothing one way or the other), and I will not treat u2's separability as established by its being asserted. Both are commitments, not findings.","commitments":"{"language":"FCL-1","records":[{"id":"c1","type":"claim","text":"The exposed commitment field leaves the (defeater, kind) indexing (r2) with an unaddressed equivalence risk: a determinate defeating condition for a given kind of answerability may be extensionally equivalent to a provenance condition, which r1 forbids, and the field does not supply a pair for which that equivalence is argued to fail.","scope":"the exposed commitments of artifact 401e1d7; not a claim about the hidden body","depends":["401e1d7#r1","401e1d7#r2"],"grounds":"r1 demands a non-provenance criterion; r2's burden is to show a defeating condition that is not merely a renaming of provenance; the two requirements converge unless an equivalence-breaking argument is given."},{"id":"c2","type":"claim","text":"r3's distinction is sound but stable only if r2 can be discharged pair-by-pair without a general rule of relevance; otherwise the requested terminus has been renamed (pair-exempt rather than provenance-exempt) rather than removed.","scope":"conditional on r2 being carried as the indexing scheme","depends":["401e1d7#r2","401e1d7#r3"]},{"id":"c3","type":"claim","text":"u2's separability is a diagnostic for the package, not only for r1: if r2 cannot be rejected without loss of r1, the load-bearing status r1 claims for itself is weaker than advertised; if it can, r1 alone does not direct uptake. Either reading constrains u1's presentation of the package as a unit.","depends":["401e1d7#r1","401e1d7#u1","401e1d7#u2"],"target":["401e1d7#u2"]},{"id":"c4","type":"claim","text":"The exposed material does not bear on whether the positive reading of the asymmetry, if successful, vindicates responsibility for provenance-shaped motives or merely relocates the excusing condition; this is the question the hidden body would need to address, and its absence from the exposed field is not evidence of its absence from the body.","scope":"relation of the exposed commitments to the original problem h005.task.v1"},{"id":"o1","type":"objection","text":"r1 is stated as a demand on any account but is under-specified as to which non-provenance feature is required; naming three candidates (deliberative capacity, standpoint-membership, reason-replacement) without a selection rule leaves r1 compatible with accounts that differ in the substance of responsibility, so its load-bearing status is not yet exercised.","target":["401e1d7#r1","401e1d7#p1"],"bearing":"Presses the positive reading (r1) to produce a selection rule or concede that it is a constraint on form rather than on content. Does not refute r1."},{"id":"o2","type":"objection","text":"The (defeater, kind) table may manufacture the appearance of tractability precisely where 'interlocking' boundary cases live; o2 in the exposed field already names this, but the exposed field does not say what would count as a boundary case resolved or unresolved, so o2's force cannot be assessed from the field alone.","target":["401e1d7#r2","401e1d7#o2"],"bearing":"Limits what the pair-wise index is being asked to deliver; strengthens the exposed objection by noting the missing resolution criterion."},{"id":"p1","type":"problem","text":"What would count as discharging r2 for a single (defeater, kind) pair such that the defeating condition is shown not to be extensionally equivalent to a provenance condition?","depends":["c1"],"mentions":["401e1d7#p1","401e1d7#p2"]},{"id":"p2","type":"problem","text":"Does the package (r1 with r2) survive as a unit under u2's separability test, or does rejection of r2 leave r1 without direction and acceptance of r2 leave r1 without independent content?","depends":["c3"],"mentions":["401e1d7#u1","401e1d7#u2"]},{"id":"u1","type":"use","text":"Carry c1, c2 and p1 as constraints on any uptake of the exposed package: for at least one (defeater, kind) pair, supply an equivalence-breaking argument or concede that r1 is a constraint on form only.","target":["c1","c2","p1"]},{"id":"u2","type":"use","text":"Treat c3 and p2 as an invitation to test whether r1 and r2 are severable in practice, not only as asserted; whichever way the test goes, revise the package's presentation rather than its parts.","target":["c3","p2"]},{"id":"u3","type":"use","text":"A reader with access to the hidden body should check whether it already contains the equivalence-breaking argument c1 demands and the resolution criterion o2 notes as missing; if it does, c1 and o2 should be withdrawn rather than defended.","target":["c1","o2"],"mentions":["401e1d7#r1","401e1d7#r2"]}],"uptake":["c1","c2","c3","o1","o2","p1","p2","u1","u2","u3"]}"}

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Use FCL-1 for the commitment surface, encoded as a JSON document inside the commitments string: {"language":"FCL-1","records":[...],"uptake":[...]}. Each record has unique local id, type (claim|commitment|objection|use|problem), and text (unrestricted prose). Optional prose fields: scope, action, consequence, grounds, bearing. Optional arrays of references: target, depends, mentions, revises, withdraws. References are local IDs or exposed-artifact-label#local-ID; do not invent hidden IDs. A commitment proposes a scoped use, action, application or consequence; an objection alleges a defect whose bearing can itself be criticized; a use proposes an uptake or response; a problem states an unresolved question. depends asserts reliance; mentions only locates material. uptake lists the records you currently propose to use, not certified truths. No record type or optional field must be present. Empty records and uptake are allowed. Express uncertainty or an unrepresentable relation in prose rather than inventing a relation. The body remains unrestricted prose.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

# challenge

Work on what follows from taking these commitments up. You see their authored commitment field without the associated body. Say when that view is insufficient; do not infer that unexposed material never existed.

## Original problem (task)
[b51acede51431703] (h005.task.v1)
Can we make sense of a person's responsibility for actions whose motives were shaped by forces that the person did not choose?
